text:
oscar: Hey team — heads up: I'm planning to move with my family to Berlin for a school year (approx 2025-08-15 to 2026-05-15). I want to keep my US homebase for comp/benefits. Qs: 1) Are we eligible for WFH stipend while abroad (whole months)? 2) Does shipping/extra equipment for a home office in Berlin get covered? 3) Any payroll/tax/social security implications for a >6 month stay? 4) Do benefits or dependent coverage change if my kid lives outside the US for >6 months? cc @maya (People Ops)
maya (People Ops): Thanks for the heads up, Oscar. This is the kind of move that definitely needs a temporary-relocation review. Short bullets: stipend can be paid but may be prorated if spanning payroll boundaries; shipping can be arranged via relocation request; >183 days triggers different residency rules in many countries so Payroll & Legal need to run checks. Please don't change homebase in HR yet. DM dates, Berlin address, passport nationalities, and whether you'll be doing any local client work.
tomas (Payroll): Flagging payroll complexity: Germany has social security and reporting obligations that can apply if an employee resides there for six months. We need exact dates and confirmation of work pattern. Also some withholding rules differ if you become a tax resident. I can run a payroll impact and PSO (social security) check once we have details.
lina (Benefits): For dependents: coverage eligibility stays based on active enrollment, but if the child becomes a local resident, certain local plans or insurer rules may change reimbursements. We'll check international coverage limits and any local provider requirements. If you enroll your child while abroad, we may need additional proof of residency for some vendors.
samir (Legal): Important: living overseas for school may raise permanent establishment (PE) concerns depending on client activity and whether you meet with customers locally. If you will host any business meetings, flag them. Also visa status matters — working on a tourist visa can be a compliance issue in some countries.
relocations-bot: relocation-case #R-3182 opened for oscar — please upload full address, passport countries, equipment list, and expected school documentation within 72 hours. Assigned to @maya.
oscar: DMing the details now: dates above, address in Charlottenburg, passports US & Argentinian, taking laptop + standing desk + 2 monitors, no local clients planned — remote work on US hours. Kid enrolled in local international school. Thanks.
maya (People Ops): Got it. I'll add expected stipend proration rules to the case and coordinate a shipping quote. Tomas & Samir — looping you into the case to run payroll/residency and PE/social security checks. Lina — can you confirm pediatric care guidance and any enrollment docs needed for the dependent? I'll post next steps in the case by EOD tomorrow.
tomas (Payroll): Will run checks; if Germany social security applies we may need to change payroll or set up voluntary coverage — I'll confirm options in the case this week.
lina (Benefits): I'll list required proof for dependent coverage while abroad and post the international provider contacts. If you need to add local medical plans we can discuss but typically US coverage continues for expat short-term arrangements.
oscar: Appreciate it, team. Will wait on the case updates and will not change homebase until cleared. :thumbsup:
